text:
Anna: Quick dump from the 1.5M-token perf sweep (g5.2xlarge) across Llama/Mistral/Mixtral/Qwen. Short tl;dr: kernel auto-selection + small batcher tweaks improved throughput for short ctx, but Qwen showed a tail-latency regression once KV cache pressure hit ~80% (context > 16k). KV eviction policy and RoPE scaling are the main suspects.

Mike: Can you post numbers? throughput / p50 / p95 per model?

Anna: Sure — highlights only here, full CSV in the perf dashboard link (posted by perf-bot below). Numbers are for 8-token warm prompt, variable context lengths: 
- Llama-2-70b: throughput 210 tok/s, p50 110ms, p95 320ms at ctx <=8k. At 32k, throughput down ~23%. Kernel switch to `fused-attn` for >8k reduced p95 by ~12%.
- Mistral-7b-Instruct: throughput 420 tok/s, p50 55ms, p95 120ms up to 16k. Stable.
- Mixtral-8x7B: throughput 340 tok/s, p50 70ms, p95 160ms. Best with `mixed-kernel-v2` for mid ctx.
- Qwen-14B: throughput 190 tok/s, p50 130ms, p95 600ms beyond 16k ctx (spiky). At 8k it's fine.

Rachel: ugh the Qwen tail sounds like KV churn. Did you try adjusting evict thresholds?

Anna: Yep. Quick A/B: default `evict_threshold=0.9` vs `0.75`. At 0.75 the p95 improved from ~600ms -> ~360ms but throughput dipped ~8% (more frequent cache misses and recompute). The interesting bit: when kernel auto-select picks the attention kernel that assumes contiguous KV layout, evict churn + small batches caused extra memcpy spikes.

Lee: Any correlation with batch size? We throttle batcher in prod to keep latency SLOs.

Anna: Strong correlation. When `max_batch_tokens` > 8192 we see kernel selection favoring larger-block kernels which are faster per-token but allocate temporary KV shards that blow past our HBM pressure point. Shorter batches (<=4096) keep memory stable but reduce throughput. There's a sweet spot per model, e.g.:
```
# suggested per-model runtime hints (starter)
qwen-14b:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  kernel_policy: prefer_latency
  kv_evict_threshold: 0.78
  rope_scale: 0.96
llama-2-70b:
  max_batch_tokens: 12288
  kernel_policy: throughput_first
  kv_evict_threshold: 0.92
  rope_scale: 1.00
mixtral-8x7b:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  kernel_policy: mixed-auto
  kv_evict_threshold: 0.85
  rope_scale: 0.98
mistral-7b:
  max_batch_tokens: 16384
  kernel_policy: throughput_first
  kv_evict_threshold: 0.9
  rope_scale: 1.00
```

Mike: That `rope_scale` tweak — did you observe generation quality deltas? We can't blindly scale RoPE without evals.

Anna: Correct — small reductions (0.96–0.98) for Qwen/Mixtral preserved BLEU/accuracy on our prompt suite (regression <0.2%) while reducing weird long-context attention bleed for >16k contexts. We ran a 2k prompt-set eval. Bigger changes start to distort position-sensitive tasks.

perf-bot: nightly-sweep: https://perf.redwood.local/sweeps/1829991111 (CSV + full traces). Attached: kernel-selection traces, KV alloc timeline, batch histogram.

Rachel: Action items I heard: (1) try ephemeral kernel hint flow for Qwen so we avoid heavy temporary KV allocations when HBM > 75%, (2) add KV evict counters + eviction-size histogram to runtime traces, (3) add a per-model recommended `max_batch_tokens` to console suggestions. Assigning: Rachel -> ephemeral hint POC, Lee -> metrics + dashboards, Anna -> update console suggestion list and run quality eval on rope tweaks.

Lee: I'll add alerting: HBM_util > 80% + kernel=fused-attn => paging risk. Also will instrument per-request KV alloc.

Mike: For rollout, prefer canary on Dedicated nodes only (so Hosted SLOs not affected). Also add automatic fallback policy: when p95 > 500ms for 5m, switch Qwen kernel_policy -> prefer_latency and reduce `max_batch_tokens` by 25%.

Anna: Agreed. I'll draft a config PR with the suggested defaults and canary plan. Will paste link here when ready.

Rachel: Nice work. TL;DR: kernel auto-select is great but we need HBM-aware hints + tuned evict thresholds per model + small RoPE scaling for Qwen-heavy long-ctx workloads.

Anna: +1 and thanks. :thumbsup:
